implementation_notes: A Scala anonymous function captures its enclosing scope, so eta-expansion matters whenever a method is passed as a value: 'xs.map(_.toInt)' vs 'xs.map(parseInt _)' vs 'xs.map(x => parseInt(x))' differ in overload resolution, which overload is picked, and what happens when parseInt takes two argument lists. Scala 3's eta-expansion rules ('using' / '?') were tightened for exactly this reason. Structural types ('{ def close(): Unit }') rely on reflection and are markedly slower than trait-based function types; prefer a named Function1/A => B.
idiom_name: anonymous function capturing enclosing scope; eta-expansion for method references; FunctionN types
pitfalls: Eta-expansion must be written deliberately: 'map(parseInt)' and 'map(parseInt _)' can resolve to different overloads than 'map(x => parseInt(x))'.
Overloaded methods are a known eta-expansion pain point; assign to a typed val first to pin the overload.
Structural types use reflection at every call and should not appear on a hot path.
Captured vars make a closure non-thread-safe; the JVM offers no automatic protection.
